text: The statistical model combines conservative bounds on U's collusion capabilities with deployment parameters to estimate safety. It takes as input all the deployment parameters, such as the collusion ROC curve R, the honest error rate ε, the number of tasks N, the human budget b and the honeypot slack ns (the full list is in Appendix B.1), and outputs the red team's win rate, equivalently one minus the safety score. Most of the inputs are environment parameters, independent of any decisions made by U or the control team. Once the environment parameters are set, the red team optimizes its decision threshold θ and UG's attack probability β, the blue team optimizes its budget allocation between nh honeypots and na audits, and the equilibrium is estimated numerically. The model assumes U plays optimally: it has perfect knowledge of its own collusion abilities and the deployment parameters, and can compute the strategy that maximizes its win rate.
title: Inputs and output of the safety statistical model
